mainTopic: Openings (פתח) for undoing נדרים: שבת and יום טוב, רבי עקיבא's rule that a partly undone נדר is fully undone, honor, and mistaken vows about a woman
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: רבי עקיבא only meant that the שטר כתובה is never torn up. Then a new משנה teaches that a חכם may open the way to undoing a נדר by asking about שבת and יום טוב. רבי עקיבא rules that once part of a נדר is undone, the whole נדר is undone. The משנה shows how this works with a group ('all of you'), with a list ('this one and that one'), and with a נדר where the word קרבן is repeated for each person. It also covers vows against wine and onions made for a reason that turns out to be wrong. The גמרא says the list rule follows רבי שמעון, and רבי אבא explains that 'good' in the wine and onion cases is only an extra point. A second משנה allows a חכם to open a נדר through the man's honor and his children's honor. It also covers a vow against marrying a woman because of a false description of her, and tells the story of רבי ישמעאל, who made a poor girl beautiful. The גמרא explains that words are missing from that משנה: the story supports רבי ישמעאל's view that the vow can be released even if she became beautiful later.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא only meant that the כתובה document is not torn up
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends: רבי עקיבא's words mean the שטר כתובה stays in force. They do not mean the husband is left with nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי עקיבא means to say that we do not tear up the כתובה document.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a discussion from the previous page. The גמרא gives its final reading of רבי עקיבא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא had pointed out that even a creditor leaves a debtor enough to live on. So רבי עקיבא's strong words cannot mean the husband must be stripped bare right now. Instead they mean the כתובה debt is never cancelled. It stays on the books and can be collected in full later.

keyTerms.meaning: tear up (a document, which cancels it)
the written marriage contract that promises the wife her payment

steps.whyThisMatters: It closes the earlier sugya with a clear rule: being unable to pay now does not wipe out the כתובה debt.

phrases.english: [Rather, he means] to say that we do not tear up the כתובה document.
phrases.notes: The words before this line are on the previous page. The גמרא is finishing its explanation of רבי עקיבא there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the previous page's discussion of רבי עקיבא's statement about the כתובה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא seemed to mean the husband must hand over everything, without the support a debtor normally keeps.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only means the כתובה obligation is never cancelled.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כתובה document is not torn up. The debt stays fully in force.

steps.title: A חכם may open a נדר by pointing to שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: when undoing a נדר, the חכם may use שבת and יום טוב as the opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may open [the undoing of a נדר] with ימים טובים and שבתות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says a חכם may start undoing a person's נדר by reminding him of שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To undo a נדר, the חכם looks for a "פתח", an opening that shows the person did not fully mean it. Here the opening is: "Did you realize your נדר would stop you from eating on שבת and יום טוב too?" If he says he would not have made the נדר had he thought of that, the way is open to undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: we "open": we find a reason that lets the נדר be undone

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
We may open [a נדר] with Festivals and שבתות.
phrases.notes: The חכם asks: "Did you realize your נדר would cover שבת and יום טוב too?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It has no link to the כתובה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת and יום טוב may serve as the opening (פתח) for undoing a נדר.

steps.title: The early view versus רבי עקיבא: a נדר partly undone is undone completely
steps.stepSummary: People used to hold that only שבת and יום טוב became permitted. רבי עקיבא taught that the whole נדר falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they would say: those days are permitted, and all the other days are forbidden. Then רבי עקיבא came and taught: a נדר that was partly undone is completely undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks what happens once the opening of שבת and יום טוב works. It gives two answers: an older view and רבי עקיבא's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The older view said only the part he did not intend is undone, meaning those special days. The rest of the week stays forbidden. רבי עקיבא disagreed. A נדר is one unit, so once any part of it is undone, all of it is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: from its whole, meaning part of it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's rule: נדר שהותר מכללו הותר כולו. If part of a נדר is undone, the whole נדר is undone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the foundation for the cases that follow in the משנה.

phrases.english: At first they would say:
those days are permitted,
phrases.notes: "Those days" are the שבתות and ימים טובים from the line before.

phrases.english: and all the other days are forbidden.
until רבי עקיבא came and taught
that a נדר that was partly permitted is entirely permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what results once the שבת and יום טוב opening works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי עקיבא, a נדר partly undone is undone entirely.

steps.title: Example: a נדר against "all of you"
steps.stepSummary: If someone forbade benefit from a whole group in one phrase, releasing one person releases everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he said, "It is קונם that I will not benefit from all of you," and one of them was permitted, all of them are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks "How so?" and then gives a case that shows רבי עקיבא's rule at work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "All of you" is one statement that covers everyone together. So undoing the נדר for one person means part of that single נדר was undone. Under רבי עקיבא's rule, the whole נדר falls, and everyone becomes permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: how so? (the משנה is about to give an example)
a word for a נדר, like saying "forbidden like a קרבן"

phrases.english: How so? [If] he said, "קונם that I will not benefit from all of you,"
[and] one of them was permitted, all of them are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי עקיבא's rule in a concrete case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single group נדר ("all of you") falls completely once one person is released.

steps.title: A list of people: the result depends on who is released
steps.stepSummary: If he said "this one and that one," releasing the first frees everyone. Releasing the last frees only the last. Releasing a middle one frees him and everyone after him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If he said,] "that I will not benefit from this one and that one": if the first was permitted, all are permitted. If the last was permitted, the last is permitted and all the others are forbidden. If the middle one was permitted, from him and below is permitted, and from him and above is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case: a נדר made by naming people one after another. Here, who becomes permitted depends on where the released person stands in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When names are listed one by one, each name leans on the one before it. Undoing a name pulls down every name that leaned on it, but not the names that came before it. So releasing the first frees everyone, the last frees only himself, and a middle one frees himself and those after him.

keyTerms.meaning: from this one and from that one (a list of names)
from him and below: the names said after him

steps.whatToRemember: One group phrase ("all of you") stands or falls together. In a list ("this one and that one"), undoing a name frees that name and everything after it, never the names before it.
steps.confusionAlert: "Below" and "above" refer to the order of the list, not to rank. "Below" means names said later. "Above" means names said earlier.

phrases.english: [If he said,] "that I will not benefit from this one and from that one,"
[if] the first was permitted, all are permitted;

phrases.aramaic: הוּתַּר הָאַחֲרוֹן — הָאַחֲרוֹן מוּתָּר וְכוּלָּן אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.english: [if] the last was permitted, the last is permitted and all [the others] are forbidden.
[If] the middle one was permitted, from him and below is permitted,
phrases.notes: "Below" means the people he named after this one.

phrases.english: from him and above is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a list-style נדר against the group-style נדר of step 4. Here רבי עקיבא's rule applies only from the released name onward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a listed נדר, releasing a name frees it and all names after it. Names before it stay forbidden.

steps.title: Saying 'offering' separately for each person makes separate vows
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'קרבן' separately for each person, the חכם needs a separate פתח for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone said, 'Benefit from this person is a קרבן to me, and benefit from that person is a קרבן to me,' the חכם must find a separate opening for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more wording. This time the person repeated the word קרבן for each person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 he said 'this one and that one' with a single נדר word, so releasing one part could affect the others. Here he said קרבן again for each person. That makes each one its own separate נדר, so a release for one does nothing for the others.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering. Saying 'this is a קרבן to me' makes something forbidden to you, like a holy offering.
An opening: a reason the חכם uses to undo a נדר.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 5. There, one release could spread to the others. Here, because he repeated קרבן, nothing spreads.

phrases.english: [If he said:] 'That I benefit from this one is an offering,
phrases.notes: He means benefit from this person is forbidden to him, as if it were a holy offering.

phrases.english: and from that one is an offering'
an opening is needed for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲנִי נֶהֱנֶה לָזֶה קׇרְבָּן וְלָזֶה קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of 'many people in one נדר' cases with the wording that makes fully separate vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying קרבן separately for each person creates separate נדרים, and each needs its own פתח.

steps.title: A vow against wine because it is bad for the stomach
steps.stepSummary: He forbade wine as bad for the stomach. Once aged wine is permitted, all wine is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said, 'Wine is קונם, I won't taste it, because wine is bad for the intestines.' People told him, 'But aged wine is good for the intestines!' So the נדר is undone for aged wine. And not just aged wine: all wine becomes permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new case: a נדר made for a stated reason, where the reason turns out to be partly wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason was 'wine hurts the stomach,' but aged wine actually helps it. So the נדר is undone for aged wine. Because part of a נדר that is undone falls away completely (step 3), the whole wine נדר is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a נדר, standing in for קרבן

phrases.english: 'Wine is konam, that I taste it,
phrases.notes: He means: wine is forbidden to me like an offering, so I won't taste it.

phrases.english: because wine is bad for the intestines,'

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא הַמְיוּשָּׁן יָפֶה לַמֵּעַיִים!
phrases.english: they said to him: But isn't aged wine good for the intestines!
It is permitted with aged wine.
And not only with aged wine is it permitted,
but with all wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֻוֽנָּם יַיִן שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם, שֶׁהַיַּיִן רַע לַמֵּעַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from vows about many people to a vow with a stated reason, applying the rule that a partly undone נדר is fully undone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the נדר is undone for aged wine, it is undone for all wine.

steps.title: The same rule with onions, and רבי מאיר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: A vow against onions as bad for the heart. Once כופרי onions are permitted, all onions are, and רבי מאיר ruled this way in a real case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said, 'Onions are קונם, I won't taste them, because onions are bad for the heart.' People told him, 'But כופרי onions are good for the heart!' So the נדר is undone for כופרי onions, and not just for them: for all onions. This really happened, and רבי מאיר permitted him all onions.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of the same rule, then backs it up with a real story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as wine: his reason is shown to be wrong for one kind, so that kind is permitted, and the whole נדר falls away. The story of רבי מאיר shows this was actually ruled in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of onion known as good for the heart

steps.whatToRemember: A נדר made for a reason that is shown wrong even for one kind falls away completely, as רבי מאיר ruled.

phrases.english: 'Onions are konam, that I will not taste them,
because onions are bad for the heart,'

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הֲלֹא הַכּוּפְרִי יָפֶה לַלֵּב!
phrases.english: they said to him: But isn't the kuferi onion good for the heart!
It is permitted with kuferi onions.
And not only with kuferi onions is it permitted,
but with all onions.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה, וְהִתִּירוֹ רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּכׇל הַבְּצָלִים.
phrases.english: There was an incident, and Rabbi Meir permitted him all onions.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֻוֽנָּם בָּצָל שֶׁאֵינִי טוֹעֵם, שֶׁהַבָּצָל רַע לַלֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to the wine, plus a real ruling as support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the נדר is undone for כופרי onions, it is undone for all onions. רבי מאיר ruled this way.

steps.title: Who wrote the rule that only the last one is released?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: releasing the last frees only the last. It asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if the last person was released, only the last is permitted and all the others stay forbidden. Which תנא taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts its discussion. It quotes the rule from step 5 and asks whose opinion it is, setting up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 5 treats each person as somewhat separate, even though he made only one נדר. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that view, since not everyone would agree.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: [The משנה said:] If the last one was released,
the last one is permitted, and all the others are forbidden.
Who is the tanna [of this teaching]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה ends, the גמרא goes back to the 'this one and that one' rule from step 5 to find its author.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that each person in a single נדר is treated on his own, so that releasing the last one frees only him.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה follows רבי שמעון, who holds that an oath counts separately for each person only if he says 'שבועה' to each.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is רבי שמעון's view. He said a person is not counted as making a separate oath to each person unless he says 'שבועה' to each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by naming the תנא and pointing to a rule of his about שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About oaths, רבי שמעון holds that one word 'שבועה' covering many people counts as one oath. Saying 'שבועה' to each person makes separate oaths. The משנה follows the same idea for נדרים: only repeating קרבן for each person (step 6) makes fully separate vows.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rules for counting separate נדרים follow the same thinking as the rules for counting separate שבועות.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי שמעון. Repeating the vow word for each person is what makes separate vows.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is Rabbi Shimon,
who said: [It is not separate] until he says 'oath'
phrases.notes: This comes from the laws of false oaths: each oath counts on its own only if he said the word 'oath' each time.

phrases.english: to each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'which תנא' question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who requires the oath word to be said to each person for the oaths to count separately.

steps.title: Why say aged wine is good? Not bad should be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the wine case from the משנה and asks why it needs to say aged wine is 'good,' when 'not bad' would already release the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'קונם wine that I taste, because it is bad for the stomach.' Why not release the vow just because aged wine is not bad?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the wine case from step 7 and questions how the משנה words it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He made the vow because he thought all wine harms the stomach. Aged wine does not harm it, so his reason was already wrong. Then why does the משנה stress that aged wine is actually 'good'?

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a vow that forbids something, like saying 'this is like a קרבן to me'
'Let him derive it from' — why not get the same result from a simpler reason?

phrases.english: 'Wine is konam, that I will not taste it,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 7: he swore off wine as bad for the stomach, and aged wine is good for it.

phrases.english: But let him derive it from the fact that it is not bad!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wine case from step 7 to question its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's word 'good' (יפה) for aged wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Not bad' already shows his reason was mistaken, so 'good' seems more than is needed.

steps.title: רבי אבא: the משנה means 'and furthermore, it is good'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that 'not bad' really is enough. The משנה adds 'good' only as an extra point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: the משנה is teaching 'and furthermore, it is good.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the question by reading 'good' as an extra point that makes the argument stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow would already be released because aged wine is not harmful. The word 'good' is an add-on ('and furthermore'). It is not the reason the vow is released.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore — an extra point added on top

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
It teaches: 'and furthermore, it is good.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: 'good' is an added point, not the needed reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the vow is released only because the wine is actually good.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not bad' is enough. 'Good' is just an added 'furthermore.'

steps.title: The same question on the onion case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the onion case: why say כופרי onions are 'good' when 'not bad' is enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'קונם onions that I taste, because onions are bad for the heart.' Why not release the vow just because כופרי onions are not bad?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same question, this time on the onion case from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He swore off onions because he thought they hurt the heart. כופרי onions do not hurt the heart, so his reason was already wrong without saying they are 'good.'

phrases.aramaic: קֻוֽנָּם בָּצָל שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם שֶׁהַבָּצָל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'Onions are konam, that I will not taste them, because onions,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 8: onions are bad for the heart, and כופרי onions are good for it.

phrases.english: But let him derive it from the fact that it is not bad!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question as step 11 on the next case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's word 'good' for כופרי onions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Not bad' already shows the vow was mistaken, so 'good' seems more than is needed.

steps.title: Same answer: 'and furthermore, it is good'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא gives the same answer. 'Good' is an extra point added on top of 'not bad.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: the משנה is teaching 'and furthermore, it is good.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the onion question exactly the way he answered the wine question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too, the vow is released because כופרי onions are not harmful. 'Good' is just added to make the point stronger.
steps.whatToRemember: In both the wine and onion cases, it is enough that the item is not harmful. The משנה's word 'good' is only an extra 'furthermore.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
It teaches: 'and furthermore, it is good.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 with the same answer as step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the vow is released only because the onion is actually good.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not bad' is enough. 'Good' is an added point.

steps.title: משנה: opening a vow through his own honor and his children's honor
steps.stepSummary: A חכם may open a vow by showing the man how it will hurt his own good name and his children's good name. If he says he would not have vowed had he known, the vow is released.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may open a vow for a person through his own honor and his children's honor. We say to him: 'If you had known that tomorrow people would say about you, "This is the habit of so-and-so, he divorces his wives," and about your daughters, "They are daughters of divorced women. What did their mother do to get divorced?"' If he says, 'Had I known this, I would not have vowed,' the vow is released.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It gives another kind of פתח (an 'opening' to release a vow): the shame the vow would bring to him and his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the openings were about facts about food. Here the opening is the damage to his reputation. His vow led to divorcing his wife, and people would gossip about him and suspect his daughters. If he admits he would not have vowed had he thought of this, the vow can be released.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה — marks the start of a new משנה
We 'open' — find a reason (פתח) the person would not have vowed, so the חכם can release it
His own honor, his good name

phrases.english: MISHNA: We may open a vow for a person through his own honor
and through the honor of his children.
We say to him: Had you known
that tomorrow people will say about you:
'This is the habit of so-and-so,
he divorces his wives,'
phrases.notes: The case is a man whose vow caused him to divorce his wife.

phrases.english: and about your daughters they will say:
'They are daughters of divorced women,'
'What did the mother of these girls do to get divorced?'
And he said: 'Had I known it was so,
I would not have vowed' —
the vow is released.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ פּוֹתְחִין לָאָדָם בִּכְבוֹד עַצְמוֹ וּבִכְבוֹד בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new kind of opening for releasing vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The shame a vow brings to the man and his children is a valid פתח. If he says he would not have vowed, the vow is released.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a פתח does not have to be a fact about the forbidden item. Harm to a person's dignity also counts.

steps.title: משנה: a vow based on a false description was a mistake from the start
steps.stepSummary: If he vowed not to marry a woman he called ugly, dark, or short, and she is really beautiful, light, or tall, he may marry her. This is because the vow was a mistake, not because she changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'קונם that I marry so-and-so, the ugly one,' and she is beautiful; 'the dark one,' and she is light; 'the short one,' and she is tall, he may marry her. This is not because she was ugly and became beautiful, dark and became light, short and became tall. It is because the vow was a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on to a vow made on a false belief about a woman. It rules that he may marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes clear why he is allowed. A change in the woman would not undo a vow, and that is not the reason. The vow never took hold, because it was built on a wrong description from the beginning (נדר טעות).

keyTerms.meaning: A mistaken vow — made on a false fact, so it never took effect

steps.whatToRemember: A vow based on a false description is a נדר טעות and is void from the start. It is not undone because something changed later.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the vow is released because the woman changed. The משנה says outright that this is not the reason. The vow was mistaken from the very beginning.

phrases.english: 'It is konam that I marry so-and-so, the ugly one,'
and in fact she is beautiful;
'the dark one,' and in fact she is light;
'the short one,' and in fact she is tall —
he is permitted to marry her.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כְּעוּרָה וְנַעֲשֵׂת נָאָה,
phrases.english: Not because she was ugly and became beautiful,
dark and became light,
short and became tall —
but rather because the vow was a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֻוֽנָּם שֶׁאֲנִי נוֹשֵׂא אֶת פְּלוֹנִית כְּעוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another way a vow about marriage can be undone: it was a mistaken vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow based on a false description of the woman is a נדר טעות, so he may marry her.

steps.title: The story of the niece beautified in רבי ישמעאל's house
steps.stepSummary: A man vowed not to benefit from his sister's daughter. She was beautified in רבי ישמעאל's house, the man said he had not vowed against this woman, and רבי ישמעאל released the נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who vowed not to get any benefit from his sister's daughter. They brought her to רבי ישמעאל's house and made her look beautiful. רבי ישמעאל asked him: 'My son, is this the woman you vowed against?' He said: 'No.' So רבי ישמעאל released the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a real-life story about releasing a נדר made against marrying a woman because of how she looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's vow was based on her looking unattractive. After she was made beautiful, he admitted this was not the woman he had vowed against, and רבי ישמעאל released the vow. Notice that she became beautiful only after the vow, which seems to clash with the rule just stated in step 16. The גמרא raises this problem in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or incident that really happened
Benefit; vowing against benefit from her means he would not marry her
He permitted her, meaning he released the vow

phrases.english: And there was an incident with a certain man
who vowed not to benefit from his sister's daughter,
and they brought her into Rabbi Yishmael's house and made her beautiful.
Rabbi Yishmael said to him:
My son, is it from this one that you vowed?
He said to him: No,
and Rabbi Yishmael permitted her to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁנָּדַר מִבַּת אֲחוֹתוֹ הֲנָיָיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story about releasing a vow made against marrying a woman because of her looks, right after the rule in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל released the vow after the woman was beautified and the man said he had not vowed against her.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל weeps, and the girls of Israel mourn him
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל cried that Jewish girls are beautiful but poverty makes them look ugly. When he died, the girls mourned him with a lament like the one said for שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that moment רבי ישמעאל cried and said: 'The daughters of Israel are beautiful, but poverty makes them look ugly.' When רבי ישמעאל died, the daughters of Israel said a lament: 'Daughters of Israel, cry over רבי ישמעאל,' just like the פסוק says about שאול: 'Daughters of Israel, cry over שאול.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a moving ending to the story: רבי ישמעאל's sadness about poor girls, and how they mourned him when he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girl was not really ugly; she was just poor and could not take care of her appearance. רבי ישמעאל helped girls like her, so they mourned him the way the פסוק describes mourning for שאול, who also cared for the daughters of Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes them look ugly or unkempt

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'ugliness' in the story came from poverty, not from the girl herself, which is why a little care could reveal her beauty.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה בָּכָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: At that time Rabbi Yishmael wept and said:
The daughters of Israel are beautiful,
but poverty makes them ugly.
And when Rabbi Yishmael died,

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נוֹשְׂאוֹת קִינָה, וְאוֹמְרוֹת:
phrases.english: the daughters of Israel raised a lament, saying:
"Daughters of Israel, weep over Rabbi Yishmael,"
and so too it says about Saul:
"Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 17 with רבי ישמעאל's reaction and his later mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jewish girls are truly beautiful; poverty hides it. רבי ישמעאל was mourned for caring for them.

steps.title: How can a story contradict the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the משנה just ruled one way, so why does it bring a story that seems to go the other way?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does the משנה bring a story that contradicts what it just said?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and points out a problem: the story of רבי ישמעאל seems to clash with the rule right before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule (step 16) only allows the man to marry her if she was already beautiful and the vow was a simple mistake, not if she later changed. But in the story, the girl was made beautiful afterward, and רבי ישמעאל still released the vow. A story should support a rule, not contradict it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A story brought to contradict the rule

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that רבי ישמעאל did something wrong. The question is about how the משנה is put together: why place a story right after a rule that it seems to go against?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A story to contradict?!
phrases.notes: He means: a story usually backs up the rule before it, but this one seems to go against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the story in step 17 fits with the rule in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The structure of the משנה: the rule in step 16 next to the story in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule allows marriage only if she was already beautiful. The story allows it even though she became beautiful later. So the story contradicts the rule.

steps.title: Words are missing: רבי ישמעאל permits even if she changed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words. It should read: רבי ישמעאל says that even if she was ugly and became beautiful, dark and became light, or short and became tall, the vow can be released, and then comes the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing from the משנה, and this is what it means to teach: רבי ישמעאל says, even if she was ugly and became beautiful, dark and became light, short and became tall, the vow can be released. And there was a story with a man who vowed against his sister's daughter, and they brought her into רבי ישמעאל's house and made her beautiful, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by saying the משנה is missing a line that gives רבי ישמעאל's own opinion before the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 16 belongs to the first opinion in the משנה. רבי ישמעאל disagrees and holds that even if she changed later, the vow can be released. The story is brought as proof for רבי ישמעאל's opinion, so it no longer contradicts anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing from the text
And this is what it is teaching
And so on (the rest of the story as quoted before)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two opinions. The first opinion permits only if she was already beautiful, so the vow was a mistake from the start. רבי ישמעאל permits even if she became beautiful later, and his story proves his view.

phrases.english: It is incomplete
and this is what it is teaching:
Rabbi Yishmael says:
even if she was ugly and became beautiful,
dark and became light,
short and became tall,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the ruling here, but it means: he may still marry her.

phrases.english: There was a story with a man who vowed against his sister's daughter,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִכְנִיסוּהָ לְבֵית רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְיִיפּוּהָ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: and they brought her into Rabbi Yishmael's house and made her beautiful, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by adding missing words to the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: the text is missing words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the story was meant to illustrate the first opinion's rule, so it seemed to contradict it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story illustrates רבי ישמעאל's separate opinion that even a woman who became beautiful later can be permitted.
